prompt: A greeting panel has a text field and a Greet button. Complete the onGreet listener method so a click sets the label to "Hello, <field text>!".
explanation: Swing components are plain Java objects: a JButton fires an ActionEvent when clicked (doClick() simulates this), and the registered ActionListener runs. Inside the listener you read state from one component with getText() and push it into another with setText(). No window is needed -- panels and components work entirely in memory, which is exactly how the tests exercise them.
hints: The listener method already runs on every click -- you only need to fill in its body.
nameField.getText() returns whatever is currently typed in the field.
Build the message with string concatenation and pass it to greeting.setText(...).
